review_note: The source's fppf descent criterion requires F sheaf, each pullback Fi an algebraic space, AND coproduct Fi itself an algebraic space; draft retains third condition rather than assuming arbitrary coproduct always exists, and defines the base-changed Fi.
statement:
Here $F_i=h_{S_i}\times_{h_S}F$ is the pullback of $F$ to the fppf cover $S_i\to S$; each asserted algebraic-space property is over the relevant base.

A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
Let $\{S_i \to S\}_{i \in I}$ be a covering of $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ is a sheaf,
\item each $F_i = h_{S_i} \times F$ is an algebraic space, and
\item $\coprod_{i \in I} F_i$ is an algebraic space.
\end{enumerate}
Then $F$ is an algebraic space.

statement:
A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $a : F \to G$ and $b : G \to H$ be
transformations of functors $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F, G, H$ are sheaves,
\item $a : F \to G$ is representable by algebraic spaces, flat,
locally of finite presentation, and surjective, and
\item $b \circ a : F \to H$ is representable by algebraic spaces.
\end{enumerate}
Then $b$ is representable by algebraic spaces.

\label{lemma-representable-by-spaces-cover}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $a : F \to G$ and $b : G \to H$ be
transformations of functors $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F, G, H$ are sheaves,
\item $a : F \to G$ is representable by algebraic spaces, flat,
locally of finite presentation, and surjective, and
\item $b \circ a : F \to H$ is representable by algebraic spaces.
\end{enumerate}
Then $b$ is representable by algebraic spaces.

review_note: The source takes an algebraic-space groupoid (U,R,s,t,c) with s,t flat lfp and j=(t,s) an equivalence relation, F=U/R algebraic space, and concludes U→F surjective flat lfp. Draft retains every groupoid and quotient hypothesis.
statement:
A morphism $a:F\to G$ of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ is **representable by algebraic spaces** when, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every morphism $h_T\to G$, the fibre-product presheaf $h_T\times_G F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$. Properties such as flatness, surjectivity, étaleness and local finite presentation of such a morphism mean that each of these base-changed morphisms of algebraic spaces has the corresponding property.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Consider an algebraic space $F$ of the form $F = U/R$
where $(U, R, s, t, c)$ is a groupoid in algebraic spaces
over $S$ such that $s, t$ are flat and locally of finite presentation, and
$j = (t, s) : R \to U \times_S U$ is an equivalence relation.
Then $U \to F$ is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-covering-quotient}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Consider an algebraic space $F$ of the form $F = U/R$
where $(U, R, s, t, c)$ is a groupoid in algebraic spaces
over $S$ such that $s, t$ are flat and locally of finite presentation, and
$j = (t, s) : R \to U \times_S U$ is an equivalence relation.
Then $U \to F$ is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation.
